## How to Get DNS Resolutions for `yahoo.com` from VirusTotal

### 1. Sign Up / Log In
- Go to the [VirusTotal website](https://www.virustotal.com/) and create an account (or log in if you already have one).
- Once logged in, navigate to your **API Key** section. You’ll need this key to authenticate your requests.

> **Tip:** The API key you mentioned (`api_key123`) looks like a placeholder. Make sure you’re using the actual key generated for your account.

### 2. Choose the Right Endpoint
For DNS resolution data, you’ll want to use the **Domain Analysis** endpoint:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}
```

Replace `{domain}` with `yahoo.com`.

### 3. Build Your Request

#### Using `curl` (Command Line)

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com" \
     -H "x-apikey: YOUR_ACTUAL_API_KEY"
```

#### Using Python (`requests` library)

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "YOUR_ACTUAL_API_KEY",
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
print(response.json())
```

> Replace `"YOUR_ACTUAL_API_KEY"` with the real key you obtained from VirusTotal.

### 4. Interpreting the Response

A successful response will look something like this (simplified):

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "yahoo.com",
    "type": "domains",
    "attributes": {
      "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
      "last_analysis_results": { ... },
      "last_dns_resolution": {
        "ip_addresses": ["98.137.246.7", "98.137.246.8"],
        "dns_records": [
          {
            "type": "A",
            "value": "98.137.246.7",
            "ttl": 300,
            "timestamp": "2024-07-28T12:34:56Z"
          },
          ...
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

- **`last_dns_resolution.ip_addresses`** – A list of IP addresses that `yahoo.com` resolved to most recently.
- **`last_dns_resolution.dns_records`** – Detailed DNS record information (record type, value, TTL, timestamp, etc.).

If you want historical DNS data, you can also query the **DNS History** endpoint:

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns_history
```

This will return a paginated list of past DNS resolutions.

### 5. Pagination & Rate Limits

- VirusTotal’s API responses are paginated. If you’re retrieving DNS history, you may need to follow the `links.next` field to fetch subsequent pages.
- Be mindful of the rate limits associated with your API key. For free keys, the limit is typically 4 requests per minute. If you hit the limit, you’ll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response.

### 6. Handling Errors

Common error responses include:
- **`404 Not Found`** – The domain isn’t present in VirusTotal’s database.
- **`401 Unauthorized`** – Invalid or missing API key.
- **`429 Too Many Requests`** – Exceeded rate limit.

Always check the HTTP status code and the `error` field in the JSON body for details.

---

## Quick Summary

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Get your real API key from VirusTotal. |
| 2 | Use the Domain Analysis endpoint (`/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com`). |
| 3 | Include the header `x-apikey: YOUR_ACTUAL_API_KEY`. |
| 4 | Parse the `last_dns_resolution` section for IPs and DNS records. |
| 5 | For historical data, use `/api/v3/domains/yahoo.com/dns_history`. |

Feel free to copy the `curl` or Python snippets above and replace the placeholder key with your actual key. That should give you the DNS resolution data you’re looking for. If you run into any specific errors or need help interpreting the JSON, let me know!
